svg.title: Dead-Letter Queue
svg.desc: Dead-Letter Queue. Park messages that keep failing so they stop blocking the queue and can be inspected. Step 1, A poison message: m-13 has a field the handler cannot parse: it fails, comes back and fails again, and the rest wait. Step 2, Park it after 3 receives: After 3 failed receives the broker parks m-13 in the dead-letter queue, and the queue flows again. Step 3, Alarm, then inspect: Depth 1 in the dead-letter queue raises an alarm. An engineer reads m-13 and fixes the handler. Step 4, Redrive: After the fix, m-13 is redriven to the source queue and saved. The dead-letter queue is empty again.

g.text: m-13 has a field the handler cannot parse: it fails, comes back and fails again, and the rest wait.
After 3 failed receives the broker parks m-13 in the dead-letter queue, and the queue flows again.
Depth 1 in the dead-letter queue raises an alarm. An engineer reads m-13 and fixes the handler.
After the fix, m-13 is redriven to the source queue and saved. The dead-letter queue is empty again.
source queue orders · delivered in order
m-14, m-15 and m-16 wait behind m-13
Same message, same code, same error:
a retry cannot fix it. Each one only
holds up the messages behind m-13.
The broker counts receives per message.
At the limit it sets m-13 aside, with
its history, and the queue moves on.
Many brokers delete its messages when
retention runs out: silent data loss.
Fix first, or m-13 just fails again.
Its work may be half done already, so
cause: a handler bug, the message is valid
